# Results — Study 881 (Jobless-Claims Sector Rotation)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: the
**4-week change in initial jobless claims** should drive a **cyclical-vs-defensive
rotation** — rising claims → tilt to **defensives** (XLP, XLU) over **cyclicals**
(XLY, XLI), so the cyclical-minus-defensive forward spread should be *negative*. Offline
& deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
Reported as-of 2026-06-30, the last complete calendar month (the partial current month
is dropped). Fingerprint `43e0a9ec1a15` (four sector-ETF closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Claims tape | FRED **`IC4WSA`** (initial claims, SA, **4-week MA**, thousands) — a documented public monthly snapshot (U.S. DoL / ETA). The FRED CSV host is **DNS-unreachable in this build**, so — as Study 385/268 do — the never-revised snapshot is encoded in `data.py` with the source cited; `fetch()` still *attempts* the live CSV (retry + DBnomics fallback). |
| Sector tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`) for **XLY, XLI** (cyclicals), **XLP, XLU** (defensives) + **SPY**, 1998-12-22 → 2026-06-30, cached under this study's own `_cache/`. **Fetched live from Yahoo.** |
| Frame | month-end alignment of the 4-week-MA claims level with month-end sector closes; **331 months**, 1998-12-31 → 2026-06-30 |
| Signal | the **4-week (≈ 1-month) change** in the 4-week-MA claims level `dcl_t = c_t/c_{t−1} − 1`; positive = claims **rising** (labour softening) |
| Outcome | equal-weight **cyclical (XLY,XLI) − defensive (XLP,XLU)** monthly return (mean **+0.251%**, sd 4.37%) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through month-end `t` → hold the spread over month `t+1` (zero look-ahead). The costed timer flips a 2×-NAV long-short book, charging one-way × NAV per leg + 50 bps/yr borrow on the short |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the predictive **slope**; R²; a 2,000-draw permutation placebo; a COVID-sensitivity / winsor / Spearman cut; a two-era split; a 20-seed synthetic control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The four SPDR sector ETFs and SPY have
traded continuously since 1998 (no delisting), so there is **no survivorship bias in the
outcome**. The *signal* is a clean public macro series. The one honest hazard is the
**single 2020 outlier**, which the robustness cut isolates below.

## The headline — predictive regression `spread_{t+1} ~ dclaims_t`

Newey-West (6-lag) regression of the forward cyclical-minus-defensive spread on the
claims change, n = **329** months:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope | **+0.0177** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* | **+6.39** |
| R² | 0.0127 |
| correlation | +0.1125 |
| **required sign for the claim** | **negative** |

The claim **fails — and inverts.** The theory predicts a *negative* slope (rising claims
→ defensives win → the cyclical-minus-defensive spread falls). The fitted slope is
**significantly positive** (+0.0177, NW *t* = **+6.39**): mechanically, a rising claims
change *precedes* cyclicals *out-earning* defensives. A significant **wrong-sign** result
is, by the desk's rule, a **None** — but the more important point is that even this
wrong-sign "significance" is a mirage of one episode, shown next.

## It is one outlier — the 2020 claims spike

| cut | slope | NW *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| full sample | +0.0177 | **+6.39** | 329 |
| **ex-COVID 2020** (drop Feb–Dec 2020) | +0.0623 | **+1.49** | 318 |
| winsorise `dclaims` at 1/99 pct | +0.0504 | **+1.43** | 329 |
| **Spearman** rank-corr (outlier-robust) | ρ = +0.0189 | *p* = **0.733** | 329 |

Removing eleven 2020 months, or winsorising the claims change, or switching to a
rank correlation, **collapses the *t* from 6.4 to ≈ 1.4 and the Spearman correlation to
≈ 0 (p = 0.73)**. In 2020 the claims 4-week MA exploded (211k → 4,174k) exactly as the
market bottomed and cyclicals ripped off that bottom — a handful of enormous
same-signed points that drag the OLS line. There is **no monotone relationship** between
the claims change and the sector rotation; the headline *t* is a single-episode
leverage artefact.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2012-01-01)

| era | slope | NW *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1999-2011 (n=156) | +0.1222 | **+1.41** | 156 |
| 2012-2026 (n=173) | +0.0164 | **+6.83** | 173 |

The only "significant" era is the one that *contains 2020*; the pre-2020 half is
insignificant (*t* = +1.41). Same story, same outlier.

## Placebo — is the fitted slope a lucky alignment?

Shuffle the claims-change column against the forward spread (breaking signal → outcome),
2,000 draws:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed slope | +0.0177 |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.00003 (0.0089) |
| two-sided *p* | **0.053** |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed slope sits at a borderline
*p* = 0.053 — i.e. barely distinguishable from a chance alignment, entirely consistent
with "one COVID episode happened to line up." A robust predictor would sit far past this;
this one does not.

## The timer — can you get paid for the rotation?

Flip a long-short cyclical/defensive book with the claim's sign (rising claims → short
the cyclical-minus-defensive spread = go defensive); one-way × NAV per leg + 50 bps/yr
borrow; 168 switches over 329 months.

| one-way cost | gross | net | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 bps** | +0.89%/yr | +0.39%/yr | +0.14 | +0.03 |
| **10 bps** | +0.89%/yr | **−1.91%/yr** | −0.66 | −0.13 |

Even *gross*, the rotation earns **+0.89%/yr** with a *t* indistinguishable from zero;
at a realistic 10 bps one-way the 168 flips turn it **negative** (−1.91%/yr). There is no
paycheck here — **Mirage**.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded frame with a *planted* rising-claims → cyclicals-underperform
relation (`edge > 0`); no network.

| world | slope NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.16** (sd 0.95), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.5`, seed 881) | slope −0.4651, **NW *t* = −13.85** |

The detector recovers a *planted* negative (claim-shaped) slope cleanly and essentially
never fires on the null — so the real-tape non-result is a genuine absence of the effect,
not a broken test. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claimed labour-nowcast rotation does **not** exist. The
  predictive slope of the cyclical-minus-defensive spread on the 4-week claims change is
  **wrong-signed** (positive, +6.39 *t*) — and that "significance" is a **single-outlier
  (COVID-2020)** artefact that collapses to *t* ≈ 1.4 ex-COVID / winsorised, to a
  Spearman ρ = +0.02 (p = 0.73), and to *t* = +1.41 in the pre-2020 era, with a
  borderline placebo (p = 0.053). A clean 20-seed synthetic control rules out a broken
  engine. Rising claims carry **no** robust cyclical-vs-defensive rotation information.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The sign-correct rotation earns only **+0.89%/yr gross**
  (*t* ≈ 0) and goes **negative** (−1.91%/yr) once its 168 flips pay a 10 bp one-way
  cost.
